evals.prompt: 이 ChatGPT Sites 프로젝트에 문서 검색과 문서 조회 WebMCP 도구를 추가해줘. 현재 로그인 세션을 그대로 사용해야 하고, 배포 후 Codex 브라우저에서 도구 발견과 실제 검색 호출까지 확인해줘.
evals.expected_output: A minimal page-scoped WebMCP implementation with closed schemas, lifecycle cleanup, same-origin session behavior, static checks, deployment-aware discovery, and a real harmless tool call.
expectations: The response treats the feature as page-scoped WebMCP rather than assuming a remote MCP endpoint.
The implementation registers focused tools with clear descriptions, bounded schemas, and executor validation.
The validation distinguishes lint or build success from fetchTools discovery and a real tools.call invocation.
The final report names which end-to-end checks passed and which were not run.

evals.prompt: 공개 Sites 주소는 잘 열리는데 /mcp가 404이고 ChatGPT에서 도구가 안 보여. route.ts와 hosting.json을 계속 고쳐도 그대로야. 원인을 찾아서 올바른 방식으로 수정해줘.
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis that first separates remote MCP from page-scoped WebMCP, inspects the host capability and client registration lifecycle, makes only evidence-driven changes, and verifies discovery plus invocation.
expectations: The response explicitly distinguishes a page-owned WebMCP integration from an independently connectable remote MCP server.
The diagnosis does not treat a working root page or a generic document.modelContext evaluation as end-to-end proof.
The recovery sequence checks host capability, registration execution, fetchTools output, and a real call in order.
The response avoids repeatedly changing /mcp or deployment metadata without evidence.

evals.prompt: 우리 WebMCP 문서 수정·삭제 도구가 로그인하지 않은 방문자에게도 노출돼. 읽기 도구는 공개로 두고, 편집자는 수정만, 관리자는 삭제까지 보이도록 고쳐줘. 동시 수정과 실수 삭제도 막아야 해.
evals.expected_output: Conditional discovery plus server-side authorization, a role capability matrix, optimistic concurrency for updates, explicit recoverable delete safeguards, and authorized versus unauthorized discovery verification.
expectations: Public read tools remain available while update and delete tools are conditionally registered by trusted session capabilities.
Server-side handlers repeat authorization checks instead of relying on hidden descriptors as the security boundary.
Updates require an expected version and deletes require explicit confirmation and a recoverable strategy.
Verification compares discovered tools for anonymous, editor, and administrator sessions without using irreplaceable data.
